songInfo.title: Landslide
songInfo.key: Eb Major (played as C Major shapes with Capo 3)

keyAndScale.primaryKey: Eb major (sounding key with capo 3; played as C major shapes)

scalesUsed.notes: C - D - E - F - G - A - B - C
scalesUsed.application: All chord voicings and fingerpicking patterns are based in open C major position relative to the capo

scalesUsed.notes: Eb - F - G - Ab - Bb - C - D - Eb
scalesUsed.application: The actual sounding pitches; the capo transposes C shapes up a minor third to Eb

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Ionian (Major) with gentle, reflective diatonic harmony
keyAndScale.keySignature: 3 flats (Bb, Eb, Ab) - sounding key; No sharps or flats for played shapes

mainProgression.description: Gentle descending and ascending bass line movement (C-B-A-B) using slash chords and the minor seventh, creating the song's flowing, introspective quality.

sectionProgressions.description: Fingerpicked pattern with a walking bass line descending from C through B to A then ascending back, creating a gentle rocking motion
Slightly more expansive harmonic movement with the subdominant F chord opening the chorus for the emotional 'landslide' vocal moments
Instrumental return to the verse pattern with the fingerpicking carrying the melody

harmonicFunction: C (I) - Tonic chord, the warm home base of the song
G/B (V/7) - Dominant chord with the 3rd (B) in the bass creating a smooth stepwise bass line from C
Am7 (vi7) - Relative minor seventh adding gentle melancholy and emotional depth
F (IV) - Subdominant chord bringing warmth and openness in the chorus sections
G (V) - Full dominant chord providing standard V-I resolution in the chorus

techniques.name: Travis Picking / Fingerpicking Pattern
techniques.description: The signature fingerpicking pattern combining an alternating bass note played by the thumb with melodic notes on the higher strings picked by the index and middle fingers

notes: C: Thumb alternates between 5th string (C) and 4th string (E), fingers pick 3rd, 2nd, and 1st strings
G/B: Thumb plays 5th string (B), fingers pick upper strings in the same pattern
Am7: Thumb alternates between 5th string (A) and 4th string (C), fingers pick upper strings
The thumb provides a steady alternating bass pulse
Index finger picks the 3rd string (G string)
Middle finger picks the 2nd string (B string)
Ring finger picks the 1st string (high E string)
sequence: Form the C chord shape and establish thumb alternation on bass strings
Add index finger picking the 3rd string on the 'and' of beat 1
Add middle finger on 2nd string and ring finger on 1st string
Combine into the flowing pattern: thumb-index-middle-thumb-index-ring
Maintain the pattern while changing chord shapes underneath
tips: Start by practicing just the thumb alternating bass notes until it becomes automatic
Add one picking finger at a time to build the pattern gradually
Keep the picking hand relaxed and anchored lightly near the soundhole
The thumb should be completely independent from the fingers
Practice the pattern on a single chord (C) until it flows before adding changes
details.progression: C - G/B - Am7 - G/B (fingerpicked with capo 3)

techniques.name: Capo Usage and Open Position Playing
techniques.description: Using a capo on the 3rd fret to play familiar open C major chord shapes that sound in the key of Eb major, making the song accessible for beginning fingerpickers

notes: Capo 3 transposes all open chord shapes up a minor third
C shape sounds as Eb major
G/B shape sounds as Bb/D
Am7 shape sounds as Cm7
F shape sounds as Ab major
G shape sounds as Bb major
This allows playing in Eb using the easiest open position fingerpicking shapes
sequence: Place capo firmly on the 3rd fret, close to the fret wire
Check tuning after placing the capo (strings may pull sharp)
Form chord shapes as if the capo were the nut of the guitar
All fret numbers are relative to the capo position
tips: Place the capo as close to the 3rd fret wire as possible
Re-tune after applying the capo for accurate pitch
Use a quality capo with even pressure for consistent tone
The open strings above the capo are critical to the song's ringing quality

techniques.name: Walking Bass Line
techniques.description: Stepwise bass note movement created by the chord progression's bass notes descending (C-B-A) and ascending (A-B-C), giving the song its flowing, continuous character

notes: C chord: bass note is C (3rd fret A string, or open with capo)
G/B chord: bass note moves down to B (2nd fret A string relative to capo)
Am7 chord: bass note continues down to A (open A string relative to capo)
The pattern then reverses: A (Am7) - B (G/B) - C (C chord)
This creates a smooth, stepwise bass motion: C-B-A-B repeating
The walking bass gives the song its gentle, rocking quality
sequence: Play C chord with thumb on 5th string (C bass note)
Move to G/B with thumb on 5th string 2nd fret (B bass note)
Continue to Am7 with thumb on open 5th string (A bass note)
Return to G/B for the ascending B bass note
The thumb traces the smooth C-B-A-B bass line throughout
tips: Focus on hearing the bass line as a separate melody underneath the picking
Keep the thumb movement smooth and connected between bass notes
The bass line should feel like a slow walk, not jumpy or staccato
This technique is the foundation of Travis picking style

sections.name: Intro
sections.description: Gentle fingerpicked introduction establishing the signature walking bass line and flowing picking pattern
notes: Begin with the thumb establishing the alternating bass pattern
Let each note ring into the next for a harp-like quality
Set a gentle, unhurried tempo at 78 BPM
The walking bass line (C-B-A-B) should be clearly audible

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: Continuing the fingerpicking pattern under Stevie Nicks' reflective vocal melody about change and the passage of time
notes: Maintain the steady fingerpicking pattern throughout
The picking should be consistent and even beneath the vocals
Allow the walking bass line to flow naturally through chord changes
Keep dynamics soft and intimate for the reflective verse mood

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: Expanded harmonic section with the F and G chords adding breadth to the emotional the signature vocal climax
notes: The F chord opens the chorus with a warmer subdominant color
Slight increase in picking intensity for emotional emphasis
The IV-I-V-vi7 movement provides a satisfying harmonic journey
Return to the verse pattern seamlessly after the chorus

sections.name: Verse 2 / Chorus 2
sections.description: Second verse and chorus cycle with Lindsey Buckingham's picking becoming slightly more confident and embellished
notes: Same fingerpicking pattern with subtle dynamic growth
The bass line walk (C-B-A-B) continues as the foundation
Slightly more assertive attack on the chorus section
The emotional arc builds naturally through the second cycle

sections.name: Outro
sections.description: Final verse pattern repetition with a gentle resolution, the fingerpicking gradually coming to rest as the song concludes
notes: Gradual decrease in picking intensity for a gentle ending
Final resolution on the C tonic chord
Let the last notes ring out naturally
The song concludes with the same intimacy it began with

guitar.recommended: Martin D-28 or similar dreadnought acoustic guitar
guitar.pickup: No pickup needed - pure acoustic tone. If amplified, use a quality acoustic pickup or microphone.

amp.recommended: Acoustic amplifier or direct PA input

effects.reverb: Very subtle room reverb if any, to preserve acoustic intimacy
effects.other: Capo on 3rd fret (essential). No effects needed. A quality capo and fresh strings make the biggest difference.

beginner.focus: Learn the chord shapes with capo and basic thumb-finger picking coordination
steps: Place capo on 3rd fret and learn the C, G/B, and Am7 chord shapes
Practice alternating bass thumb pattern on each chord separately
Add one finger (index on 3rd string) to the thumb pattern
Work on smooth chord transitions while maintaining the thumb pattern

intermediate.focus: Master the full fingerpicking pattern and play through the entire song
steps: Add middle and ring fingers to complete the Travis picking pattern
Practice the pattern at 78 BPM with a metronome
Learn the F and G shapes for the chorus section
Play through the entire song structure with correct fingerpicking

advanced.focus: Add dynamics, embellishments, and sing along while picking
steps: Add subtle dynamic variation between verse and chorus
Experiment with occasional hammer-ons and pull-offs within the pattern
Practice singing the melody while maintaining the fingerpicking
Develop personal expression and phrasing within the picking pattern

commonMistakes: Losing the alternating bass thumb pattern during chord changes
Picking fingers getting out of sync with the thumb
Rushing the tempo - Landslide should feel unhurried and flowing
Muting the open strings that need to ring as part of the chord
practiceRoutine: Warm up with single-chord fingerpicking on C for 5 minutes (thumb only first, then add fingers)
Practice the chord transitions C to G/B to Am7 with just the thumb pattern
Add the full fingerpicking pattern to the chord transitions
Play through the verse progression at slow tempo, gradually increasing to 78 BPM
Run through the complete song including the chorus section
focusAreas: Thumb independence from the picking fingers
Smooth chord transitions without breaking the picking pattern
Even volume and tone across all picked notes
Walking bass line clarity beneath the melodic picking
metronomeWork: Start at 50 BPM with just the alternating thumb bass pattern
Add picking fingers at 50 BPM, increasing in 5 BPM increments
Reach 78 BPM (song tempo) with the complete pattern
Practice without metronome to develop natural rubato feel once pattern is solid
